body.text: This is your question for today. Keep it in mind during the games.
Three games tonight: standing, guarded, pinned. Win one and the next round gets harder. Lose it and you run the same one again.
2v1 Hand Fight to Underhook to Close Hand Connection
Skill Learning Objective (SLO): Entering, for both players.
Both players stand facing each other, hand fighting range, both fully disconnected.
Get two connections on any two of your partner's wrist, elbow, or head, get the underhook, then go straight from there to closing both hands around his leg, body, or head.

items: Whoever connects first wins. The same rule applies to both players.

body.text: Open Guard Takedown and Escape Game
SLO: Arriving for the top player, Leaving for the bottom player.
The top player stands. The bottom player is on his back, fully connected, hands on the top player's ankles, feet inside his legs.
Bottom player: stay connected while putting the top player down on his hips or hands, then stand up, or stay connected as he rises. Top player: break the connections and make shin contact to pass.

items: The bottom player wins by putting the top player down and getting up to standing, or by putting him down a different way and rising to a connection.
The top player wins with shin contact.

body.text: Chest to Back to Precursor Transitions Game
SLO: Finishing for the top player, Leaving for the bottom player.
The top player is behind the bottom player with chest-to-back contact.

Top player: keep chest-to-back with your hands or hooks, or move to a precursor position on top, staying under an elbow while you move. Bottom player: put your back on the mat with nothing under your elbows, or turn face to face.

items: The top player wins by reaching a precursor position on top. Chest to back by itself is a continuous hold, no time count, and if the bottom player escapes, you reset.
The bottom player wins by his back on the mat or by turning face to face.

slides.title: How you win it
slides.question: In Chest to Back to Precursor Transitions Game, what wins it for the top player?

options.text: The top player wins by reaching a precursor position on top. Chest to back by itself is a continuous hold, no time count, and if the bottom player escapes, you reset.
options.feedback: That is the win condition, and nothing else scores.

options.text: Holding the finish after your partner taps
options.feedback: Never. You let go the second your partner taps. Every single time. The tap is law.

options.text: Hurting your partner because you can
options.feedback: That is the one thing the Back Pin teaches you never to do. Total control, plus the choice not to hurt someone, is the heart of the whole program.

slides.correctText: That is how you win today.
